Running in offline (file://) mode — legacy renderer active
You opened this page from your filesystem, so the browser blocks fetch() for security. The app can't load the official Annex D symbol library (236 SVG files), fonts, or portrayal catalogue, so it's falling back to the built-in hand-drawn renderer. Parsing, validation, and GML generation still work — only the preview symbols differ.
To see the official Annex D symbols, start a local server from this folder and open the app via http://localhost:8080. On Windows, double-click start-server.bat; on macOS/Linux, run ./start-server.sh. Or manually:
cd <path-to-this-folder>
python3 -m http.server 8080
# then open:  http://localhost:8080/s201_aton_studio.html
Any static file server works: python3 -m http.server 8080, npx http-server -p 8080, php -S localhost:8080, VS Code "Live Server" extension, etc.

Compare two deliveries

Load two S-201 datasets (.gml) or two full Exchange Sets (.zip) — or paste GML text — and see what changed: features added, removed, or modified (field-level old → new), discovery-metadata changes, and each file's SHA-256 delivery-integrity checksum. S-201 editions are whole replacements (PS 2.0.0 §8.1), so this diff IS the change record between edition A and edition B. Everything runs locally — nothing is uploaded.
A — earlier / reference
B — later / received
Load or paste both sides, then click Compare A → B.

Excel → S-201

Most producer AtoN lists are spreadsheets whose columns sit in a different order every time. Load a workbook (.xlsx/.xlsm), a .csv/.tsv, or paste cells copied from Excel; say what each column means; convert. The converted dataset goes to the Builder, the Validator, the Drawing tab, or a .gml file — and every decision that was not a plain copy of a cell is listed in the conversion report.
